reviewSummary: REJECT at 2 unlabeled MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Custody, payload bytes, the four required non-Windows copies, live anchors, permitted cited-input digests, platform quotations, leftover-design standing, and protected-row denials measure clean. The subject nevertheless contains two independent operative contradictions. First, $.basedOn.sarifLeftoverJoinV14.role names basedOn.d355.role as the sole last-heading claimant even though live and dispatched custody is D-357, $.basedOn.d355.role denies last-heading standing, and the rest of the subject assigns sole custody to $.basedOn.d357.role. Second, $.doesNot[19] denies authoring per-platform copies and $.failsIf[26] makes a per-platform authorship claim fatal, while the purpose, whatIsAuthored, authored catalog, physical corpus, and summary all say that g21-fixture-corpus.v32 authors those four copies. The latter guard is therefore triggered by the subject's own core claim.

Elsewhere the subject correctly says $.basedOn.d357.role is the sole claimant. The artifact therefore contains incompatible custody claims and lands the prompt's explicit sole-claimant attack.

The contradictory d355 reference occurs in an operative basedOn role, not merely in a failsIf guard or a quotation of rejected text.

Those statements conflict with the artifact's central claim: $.purpose says to author the copies, $.whatIsAuthored names four copies, the authored catalog enumerates them, $.summary.platformCopiesAuthored is true, and all four files exist at the catalogued paths. Because the dispatch fixes the speaker as g21-fixture-corpus.v32, the artifact's own affirmative fields trigger $.failsIf[26].

The two negating entries are therefore not a harmless binds-NOTHING disclaimer: they contradict the proposal's declared authored surface.
